subject: Azure marketplace: structured bundle BOM & channel margin request
messages:
From: Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the autoscaling examples. We are preparing an internal purchase request and would like to route a private offer via Azure Marketplace.

Attached is our initial bill of materials (BOM_Acme_v3.xlsx) showing expected consumption by SKU over 12 months and a preferred packaging split (core inference + enterprise observability add-on). A few asks:
- Can Redwood provide a list price (per-SKU) and an anchored private-offer discount that preserves a 22% reseller margin to our distributor?
- Are you open to a tiered list-price schedule (e.g., commit bands) so our finance team can show projected cost reductions at scale?
- Any constraints on combining your reserved-capacity seat SKUs with marketplace metered SKUs?

We'd like a target deadline of Thursday EOD to include numbers in our procurement packet. If helpful, loop in the AWS marketplace contact copied.

Thanks,
Jenna Park
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Analytics

Attachment: BOM_Acme_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Hi Jenna — thanks for the BOM and the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes on private offer, yes on tiered list pricing, and we can structure a reseller pass-through that preserves ~22% margin depending on final SKU mix.

I'll do a first-pass price carve with Ben (handling channel) and Laura (legal/contract). A couple clarifying questions before we lock numbers:
- In the BOM you labeled "observability add-on" as metered usage. Do you want that to be a separate marketplace SKU or a single combined bundle SKU? Combining gives a simpler PO but limits per-component consumption visibility.
- Are you expecting a 12-month prepaid commit for reserved capacity, or month-to-month metered purchases for the inference SKU?

I'll aim to get a proposed price schedule to you by Wed 16:00 PT. If that timeline slips we'll flag it immediately.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Connor / Jenna — quick note on channel margin math and marketplace mechanics.

If Acme wants a distributor to capture a 22% margin, we need to set our marketplace list prices such that: (List price - marketplace fee - distributor margin) >= Redwood net target. Marketplace fees vary but assume ~8% for Azure public marketplace. That means our list price should be ~1.33x the net to make the math work for a 22% pass-through after fees.

Practical approach I recommend:
1) Create two SKUs in marketplace: a combined "Core + Observability" bundle (for ease of procurement) and a standalone metered observability SKU (for telemetry visibility).
2) Offer a private-offer discount applied to the combined bundle; leave the metered observability at list (or small discount) so distributor margin flows predictably.
3) For commit tiers, we can publish a stepped list price with private-offer effective discounts for each band.

Connor: I'll draft the per-SKU list price targets and include a sample margin waterfall in the spreadsheet.

Ben Carter
Head of Channel Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Thanks Ben — that waterfall approach makes sense. A couple more specifics from our side:
- The distributor requires explicit line-item evidence of the margin; can you include a simple "margin waterfall" tab in the BOM?
- For governance we prefer reserved capacity on the core inference SKU (12-month commit) and metered for observability. Can Redwood map commit-band price tiers to a private-offer code we can attach to the PO?

Also, can you confirm whether Azure will allow a single private-offer document that references two SKUs (one reserved, one metered) under the same offer ID? AWS has historically been flexible, but we know Azure is sometimes stricter.

-Jenna
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Hi Jenna — quick update and proposed next steps. Attached is a revised BOM with the margin waterfall and two SKU approach (BOM_Acme_v3.xlsx, tab "margin_waterfall"). Highlights: 
- Proposed list prices (core reserved SKU): $0.062/token-hour equivalent (list).
- Observability metered SKU: $0.015/metric-unit (list), kept at small discount so distributor margin is preserved.
- Private-offer discount for the combined bundle: 18% at baseline commit band (gives distributor ~22% after marketplace fees and pass-through).

Azure private-offer mechanics: we confirmed with the marketplace contact that Azure supports multi-SKU private offers under one offer ID as long as the offer metadata ties the SKUs together. Amazon/AWS allowed the same historically; I'll include a note in the private-offer template.

Next actions:
- Laura to review the private-offer T&Cs for revenue recognition and resale clauses (cc'd).
- Marcus to validate tax and invoice routing for the distributor flow.
- Jenna: confirm the commit band you expect (we used the mid band from your BOM for the initial numbers).

If that looks OK I can start paperwork and generate the Azure private-offer draft (using Azure_Private_Offer_Template.pdf) for review by Thu EOD.

Connor

Attachment: Azure_Private_Offer_Template.pdf (1 page template)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Connor / Jenna — I reviewed the draft private-offer flow. Two quick items:
1) We need to add an explicit reseller pass-through clause that states the distributor is authorized to invoice Acme and retain the negotiated margin. I'll draft language and attach a one-pager.
2) For revenue recognition we prefer Azure invoices to be routed directly to Redwood's billing system (we'll then pass-through the distributor payment as appropriate). If Acme requires a different tax flow, flag Marcus to prepare tax routing options.

I'll send the clause language by EOD and attach it to the private-offer PDF. Once Jenna confirms the commit band we can finalize.

Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Park <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer for structured bundle (BOM attached)

Connor — this looks good. Acme confirms the mid commit band and we agree to proceed with the combined bundle private offer referencing both SKUs. The distributor margin waterfall looks correct to us.

Please proceed to generate the private-offer draft and share the DocuSign when ready. Our procurement team will route for signature once we have the private-offer ID and final line items.

Appreciate the quick turn-around.

Jenna Park
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Analytics
